summary: Izumi Hoshi is a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics who studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1986 to 1995. She served as an associate professor at the Tokyo University of Foreign Studies from circa 2001 to 2017.
Izumi Matsuda-Kiami works in the fields of linguistics and Japanology. Educated at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, she later held an academic post at the University of Washington.

J. A. B. van Buitenen was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Utrecht University (~1946–1953) under Jan Gonda (~1948–1953). He held posts at Utrecht University (~1953–1956) and the University of Chicago (~1959–1979).

J. B. Disanayaka is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He held an academic post at the University of Colombo from circa 1968 to 2002, as well as an attested post at SOAS University of London in 1996.

J. C. Cleary was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Harvard University (~1973–1980) under doctoral supervisor Masatoshi Nagatomi. He served as an instructor at Wesleyan University.

J. Estlin Carpenter was a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied at the University of London from circa 1860 to 1866. He later held an academic post at the University of Oxford from circa 1886 to 1915.
J. G. de Casparis was an Indology and history and archaeology scholar. He held a professorship at Leiden University (attested 1987) and a post at SOAS University of London (attested 1991).

Religious studies scholar J. Gordon Melton studied at Birmingham–Southern College, Garrett-Evangelical Theological Seminary, and Northwestern University. His posts include directing the Institute for the Study of American Religion (~1969) and positions at UC Santa Barbara (~1985–2011) and Baylor University (~2011).
J. Talboys Wheeler worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. After studying at the University of Oxford, he served as Assistant Secretary for the Government of India from circa 1862 to 1870.
Jack Kornfield is a specialist in Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied at Dartmouth College from circa 1963 to 1967. He held a post at the Spirit Rock Meditation Center around 1987.
Jack Laughlin is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who completed his PhD at McMaster University in 1999. He subsequently held an academic post at the University of Sudbury.

Jacob Dalton works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, earning his PhD at the University of Michigan under Donald S. Lopez Jr. He held positions at SOAS, Yale University (2005), and the University of California, Berkeley (attested 2011).
Jacob Holubeck is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Jurievitch Solonin, attested in 2013.

Jacob N. Kinnard is a scholar in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He has held academic appointments at William & Mary as Assistant Professor of Religion and at the Iliff School of Theology.

Indologist Jacob Samuel Speyer studied under Hendrik Kern (~1868–1872). He held academic posts at the University of Amsterdam (1877–1889), the University of Groningen (1889–1903), and served as Professor of Indology at Leiden University (1903–1913).

Jacob Wackernagel was a linguistics and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Göttingen under Theodor Benfey (~1872–1874). He held professorships at the University of Basel (1881–1902) and the University of Göttingen (~1902–1915).

Jacqueline I. Stone works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, having studied at SFSU and UCLA. She was president of the Society for the Study of Japanese Religions (~1996–1999) and a professor at Princeton University (~1990–2019).

Jacqueline Suthren Hirst specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy, completing her doctoral studies under Julius Lipner. She held an academic post at the University of Manchester, attested in 2005.

Jacques Bacot was a scholar in Tibetology and linguistics. During his career, he held academic appointments at the University of Paris and at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from circa 1936 to 1948.

Jacques Gernet studied at the University of Algiers 1 and École nationale des langues orientales vivantes. A scholar of Sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, he held posts at CNRS, EHESS, Sorbonne, Paris Diderot, and Collège de France (1975–1992).
